sources.title: BrainBread 2 Dedicated Server - AppID 475370 [RELEASED] - official Steam announcement

BrainBread 2 source - GameBase_Server.cpp: admin_kick_id forwards 'kickid %i "%s"' (USERID), admin_ban_id forwards 'banid %i %i' (minutes, USERID) then 'kickid' then 'writeid;writeip'; IsValidAdmin() returns false when UTIL_GetCommandClient() is null; admins.txt read from data/settings/admins.txt
SourceMod smn_banning.cpp - issues 'banid %d %s' with a Steam auth string, 'removeid %s', 'addip/removeip', each followed by 'writeid'/'writeip' for permanent bans
SourceMod PlayerManager.cpp - kicks with 'kickid %d %s' (USERID, unquoted message)
Setting up Dedicated BrainBread 2 Game server - Steam guide (brainbread2server\brainbread2\cfg\server.cfg, port 27015)

Rcon / Console Commands - BrainBread 2 Help & tips (dev Wuffesan: 'to use admin_ commands, you have to set yourself as an admin ... admins.txt file under data/server/'; thread does not confirm RCON itself)
game.KickID - Garry's Mod Wiki (Source-engine kickid wrapper: 'UserID, SteamID or SteamID64 of the player to kick')
Console Command List - Valve Developer Community (lists kick, kickid, banid, removeid; one-line descriptions only, no parameter syntax)

notes: BrainBread 2 (Reperio Studios, free standalone game appId 346330) ships a separate dedicated-server tool app, appId 475370 (the developer's own Steam announcement, SteamDB and LinuxGSM agree), which is plain srcds built on Source SDK 2013 Multiplayer: LinuxGSM's bb2server runs './srcds_run -game brainbread2 -strictportbind -ip <ip> -port 27015 ... +servercfgfile <cfg>'. The command channel is therefore stock Valve Source RCON (TCP) on the game port; hostport is the cvar, normally set with the -port launch argument, and RCON is enabled by setting rcon_password in brainbread2/cfg/server.cfg. No -usercon flag appears in LinuxGSM's start parameters or the Steam setup guide, and SDK 2013 servers do not require one - but note that no source found actually demonstrates an RCON session against BB2; the transport is inferred from it being unmodified srcds. Every command recorded is an ENGINE command: status, kickid, banid, removeid, writeid, say. BrainBread 2's own admin_kick_id, admin_ban_id, admin_changelevel, admin_spectate and admin_joinhuman are deliberately NOT recorded: GameBase_Server.cpp routes each through IsValidAdmin(), which begins 'if (!pClient || pClient->IsBot()) return false' on ToHL2MPPlayer(UTIL_GetCommandClient()), so issued over RCON - where there is no command client - they silently do nothing. Those same functions are the evidence that the engine commands are live on this build: admin_kick_id forwards 'kickid %i "%s"', admin_ban_id forwards 'banid %i %i' then 'kickid' then 'writeid;writeip', and the ban-list check forwards 'kickid %i You're on the ban list!' unquoted. SourceMod corroborates independently: smn_banning.cpp issues 'banid <minutes> <steam auth string>' and 'removeid <steam auth string>', each followed by 'writeid' when the ban is permanent, and PlayerManager.cpp kicks with 'kickid %d %s'. CONFIDENCE IS LOW FOR ONE SPECIFIC REASON: every primary source that actually kicks does so BY USERID ('kickid %i ...' in BrainBread 2, 'kickid %d %s' in SourceMod, and community command references describe kickid as taking a user ID), while this file templates kickid with a Steam ID. The Steam-ID form rests on the engine's documented 'userid or uniqueid' behaviour and on Garry's Mod's game.KickID ('UserID, SteamID or SteamID64'), neither of which was checked against this build; the Valve Console Command List entries are one-line descriptions with no parameter syntax and corroborate nothing about the forms. banid and removeid with a Steam ID ARE confirmed by two independent code sources. If kick misses, the userid is available as accountId from status and 'kickid <userid> <reason>' is the confirmed fallback. Until someone runs these against a live server (verifiedAt is still null), treat kick as the weak link. banid is 'banid <minutes> <userid|uniqueid> {kick}', 0 minutes = permanent, and has no reason argument natively, so {reason} is deliberately absent from the ban template; the trailing literal 'kick' makes it also disconnect the player. IMPORTANT: banid and removeid only change the in-memory list; run 'writeid' afterwards to rewrite brainbread2/cfg/banned_user.cfg, or the change is lost on restart (BrainBread 2's own ban command and SourceMod both do exactly this). One documented disagreement on quoting: BrainBread 2's source quotes the kick reason ('kickid %i "%s"') while SourceMod and BB2's own ban-list kick leave it unquoted, and srcds admins report that quoting makes the quotes show up literally in the message; the reason is recorded unquoted because kickid takes the remainder of the line either way. playerId is the Steam ID rather than the per-session userid because it is the Steam ID that banned_user.cfg persists and that removeid needs, and because the userid is not stable across reconnects - at the cost of the kick caveat above. The status uniqueid column was not observed on this specific SDK 2013 build, so the pattern accepts both the legacy STEAM_0:1:x form and the modern [U:1:x] form; it is wrapped in a non-capturing group so that anchoring it does not split the alternation. playerParse maps the userid column to accountId, which is the id BrainBread 2's own in-game admin commands use. The developer's Steam post gives the admins.txt path as data/server/, while current code reads data/settings/admins.txt. There is no motd command - Source serves brainbread2/motd.txt - so motd is omitted.
